info.description: The Klaviyo REST API. Please visit https://developers.klaviyo.com for more details.

post.description:
> 🚧 This endpoint is in beta and subject to change. > > A beta revision header (2026-10-15.pre) is required to use our beta APIs. Klaviyo APIs in beta are not intended for use in production. See our [versioning and deprecation policy](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/api_versioning_and_deprecation_policy) for more information. Get totals for a live event. Returns how many people your campaigns for the event reached on each channel, and in-store sales during the event. Set `filter.live_event_id` to the event, and set the timeframe to `{"key": "all_time"}`. Other timeframes aren't supported: reach always counts every campaign sent for the event, and sales always cover the event's start and end time. To get sales for one host location, also set `filter.location_id`. You can't combine this filter with reach statistics.

*Rate limits*:
Burst: `3/s`
Steady: `60/m` **Scopes:** `locations:read` [OpenAPI Spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaviyo/openapi/main/openapi/beta/apis/query_location_values_beta.json)

See our [versioning and deprecation policy](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/api_versioning_and_deprecation_policy) for more information. Time-bucketed series for one or more statistics. ``social_subscribers`` requires ``filter.channel``. The funnel statistics (``funnel_started``, ``funnel_submitted_identifier``, ``funnel_ended``) require ``filter.automation_id`` and can't be combined with ``social_subscribers`` in one request. A statistic that is not yet available returns ``422`` with code ``statistic_not_yet_available``.

*Rate limits*:
Burst: `3/s`
Steady: `60/m` **Scopes:** `social:read` [OpenAPI Spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaviyo/openapi/main/openapi/beta/apis/query_social_series_beta.json)

See our [versioning and deprecation policy](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/api_versioning_and_deprecation_policy) for more information. Point-in-time aggregate statistics, optionally broken down by dimension. Omit ``dimension`` for a single account-level row, or set it to ``content``, ``creator``, or ``auto_reply`` for one row per item. The revenue statistics (``social_revenue``, ``auto_reply_revenue``, ``engagement_revenue``) can't be combined with a dimension. An invalid statistic / dimension combination returns ``422`` with code ``invalid_statistic``; a combination that is not yet available returns ``422`` with code ``statistic_not_yet_available``.

*Rate limits*:
Burst: `3/s`
Steady: `60/m` **Scopes:** `social:read` [OpenAPI Spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaviyo/openapi/main/openapi/beta/apis/query_social_values_beta.json)

post.description:
> 🚧 This endpoint is in beta and subject to change. > > A beta revision header (2026-10-15.pre) is required to use our beta APIs. Klaviyo APIs in beta are not intended for use in production. See our [versioning and deprecation policy](https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/api_versioning_and_deprecation_policy) for more information. Ask a question about your account data in plain language and get a plain-language answer. K-SQL turns your question into read-only queries over your account's data, runs them, and summarizes the results. The result sets behind the answer are included so you can see how it was reached. If the question is too ambiguous to answer, `status` is `clarification` and `answer` contains a question for you. Ask again with more detail. An answer can only draw on data that your API key or OAuth token has scopes for. Each request uses Composer AI Credits. This API is available to accounts that have been enabled for it. Answers can take several seconds, so allow for this in your client's request timeout.

*Rate limits*:
Burst: `1/s`
Steady: `15/m` **Optional Scopes:** `campaigns:read` `catalogs:read` `events:read` `lists:read` `metrics:read` `profiles:read` `segments:read` [OpenAPI Spec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaviyo/openapi/main/openapi/beta/apis/ask_analytics_question_beta.json)

requestBody.description: A natural-language question about your account data.

question.description: The natural-language question to ask. 1-2000 characters.
question.example: How many orders were placed last week?

max_rows.description: Cap on rows per result set. 1-1000.

status.description: Whether this ask was answered or needs more input.

answer.description: Plain-language answer when `status` is `success`, or the clarifying question back to the caller when `status` is `clarification`.

result_sets.description: The executed queries' typed result sets supporting `answer`. Always empty when `status` is `clarification`; may also be empty on `success` when the answer required no query execution.

warnings.description: Caveats that change how `answer` and `result_sets` should be read -- a sampled result set, row data elided by a cap, a table withheld from this ask. Several conditions are reported nowhere else, so surface these alongside the answer rather than discarding them.
example: Showing the first 100 of 4,182 matching orders.

id.description: Identifier for this ask, for joining logs across services.

type.description: The column's data type. It determines how the column's values appear in `rows`.

columns.description: The result set's columns, in the order their values appear in each row.

rows.description: The result rows. Each row is a list of values in the same order as `columns`. A value is a boolean for `boolean` columns, a number for `long` and `double` columns, and a string for every other type. A missing value is `null`.

row_count.description: The number of rows in the query's result.

rows_returned.description: The number of rows included in `rows`. This is lower than `row_count` when row data was left out by a cap.

completeness.description: Whether the QUERY's result was complete -- it says nothing about this payload. `sample` means the query's row count equalled its own `LIMIT`, so the underlying result may be larger; `truncated` means it hit K-SQL's own result cap. Compare `rows_returned` to `row_count` for payload elision, which is separate: `complete` with `rows_returned` below `row_count` is a full query result only partially included here.

description.description: A short plain-language description of what this result set contains.
description.example: Order count and average price for last week.

sql.description: The K-SQL query that produced this result set, so you can see how the numbers were derived. Read-only and for explanation only: it is not a stable interface while K-SQL is in alpha -- do not parse it or store it. To run a K-SQL query yourself, see `POST /api/ksql-query`.
sql.example: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE placed_at >= '2026-09-01'

caveats.description: Caveats about this result set, in plain language and safe to show an end user as sent. The same sentences also appear in the response-level `warnings`; read them here when you need to know which result set a caveat applies to.
example: Showing the first 100 of 4,182 matching orders.

start.description: First day to include, in the account's timezone.

end.description: Last day to include, in the account's timezone.

groupings.description: The location this series belongs to.

statistics.description: Each requested statistic, with one value per day in `date_times`. Null if the statistic isn't available for this location.

location_id.description: The location to report on. Required.

statistics.description: Statistics to return for each day. `revenue` is sales after refunds (`gross_revenue` minus `refunds`). `purchasers` counts unique buyers per day, so adding up days can count the same buyer more than once.

timeframe.description: The days to report on. Use a preset `key` or a `start` and `end` up to 365 days apart. `all_time` isn't supported.

interval.description: How to group the results. Only `day` is supported.

date_times.description: The start of each day in the report, in the account's timezone.

id.description: Opaque identifier for this report response.

LocationSeriesStatistic.description: In-store statistics for a location, one value per interval.

groupings.description: The live event, and the host location if you filtered by one.

statistics.description: Each requested statistic and its value. Null if it isn't available.

live_event_id.description: The live event to report on. Required.

location_id.description: Only count sales at this host location. Can't be used with reach statistics.

statistics.description: Statistics to return. `email_reach`, `sms_reach`, and `push_reach` count the people your campaigns for this event reached on each channel. `whatsapp_messages_delivered` counts messages, not people. Someone reached on two channels is counted on both, so don't add the channels together. `gross_revenue`, `purchasers`, and `order_count` are in-store sales during the event.

timeframe.description: Must be `{"key": "all_time"}`. Reach always counts every campaign sent for the event, and sales always cover the event's start and end time.

filter.description: Which live event to report on.

id.description: Opaque identifier for this report response.

start.description: ISO-8601 lower-bound (inclusive) for the report window.

end.description: ISO-8601 upper-bound (exclusive) for the report window.

id.description: Bucket start date (ISO-8601), unique within the response.

statistics.description: Map of statistic key -> value for this bucket.

channel.description: Subscriber-growth channel to scope social_subscribers to. Required when requesting social_subscribers; ignored otherwise.

automation_id.description: Scopes funnel_started/funnel_submitted_identifier/funnel_ended to one auto-reply automation. Required for those statistics.

statistics.description: Statistics to compute per time bucket.

id.description: Opaque identifier for the series report response.

groupings.description: Bucket-identifying values for this row. Empty when the request omits a dimension for a single account-level row. dimension=content rows also include 'posted_date' (YYYY-MM-DD) when available.

statistics.description: Computed metrics for this row. Only the statistics named in the request appear here. A value is null when the aggregate has no data to report (e.g. no post reported a value) rather than being omitted.

content_type.description: Restrict dimension=content rows to owned or user_generated content. Ignored for every other dimension. Omit to rank across both.

statistics.description: Statistics to compute. Combine multiple in one call to receive all of them per row.

dimension.description: Optional breakdown dimension. Omit for a single account-level row. Not valid combined with any revenue statistic (engagement_revenue, auto_reply_revenue, social_revenue).

sort.description: Sort key when dimension is set; prefix '-' for descending. Ignored otherwise.

page_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page of results.

page_size.description: Rows per page. Only applies when dimension is set.

id.description: Opaque identifier for the values report response.

SocialValuesStatistic.description: Metrics computable for each social values-report row.

Klaviyo-API-Key.name: Authorization
Klaviyo-API-Key.description:
Private key authentication for /api/ endpoints is performed by setting the `Authorization` header to `Klaviyo-API-Key your-private-api-key`
For more information please visit https://developers.klaviyo.com/en/v2026-10-15.pre/reference/api-overview#authentication
